what: IonQ builds quantum computers using trapped ions: individual charged atoms held in place by electric fields and manipulated with lasers. It sells access to them through cloud providers and sells systems outright.
customers: Research institutions, government laboratories, and companies experimenting with quantum algorithms.
money: quantum computing time sold through Amazon, Microsoft and Google clouds
hardware sold to governments and research centres
moat: Trapped-ion qubits hold their state far longer than the superconducting kind, which is a genuine technical advantage, and IonQ has more operating systems in the field than other trapped-ion firms.
risks: $688M of negative free cash flow: this company consumes cash, it does not generate it
28 times sales on $380M of revenue, most of which is research contracts rather than commercial use
No one yet knows which quantum technology will win, or when quantum computers will be commercially useful
opportunities: $2.4B of cash against $30M of debt, which funds years of development
Revenue grew from $2M to $130M in four years and is $380M over the last twelve months
Analysts see about 139% upside, though with enormous disagreement, and governments keep funding quantum programmes
watch: Bookings and the technical roadmap milestones on qubit count and fidelity.
